# Introduction

::: {.callout-tip title="Video lecture"}
David Rocke's Epi 204 lecture
[*Introduction to Logistic Regression*](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-2021-03-30.mp4)
([slides](https://dmrocke.ucdavis.edu/Class/EPI204-Spring-2021/EPI204-1%20Introduction%20to%20Logistic%20Regression.pdf))
opens with this chapter's material:
risk estimation,
[risk ratios](#def-RR) versus [odds ratios](#def-OR),
and which of them each study design can estimate
[@rocke2021epi204].
:::

::: notes
This chapter reviews measures of association for [binary outcomes](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/data.html#def-binary-var):
risks, [risk differences](#def-RD), risk ratios, [odds](#def-odds), and odds ratios,
along with the [logit](#def-logit-fn) and [expit](#def-expit) functions that connect
probabilities, odds, and [log-odds](#def-logodds).
These concepts are the vocabulary for [regression models](Intro-to-GLMs.qmd#def-regression-model) of binary outcomes;
the [logistic regression chapter](logistic-regression.qmd) builds on them.
:::
